questions.prompt: What should Regesto mean by supporting an agent?
questions.description: Equal automatic behavior is impossible for hosts without hooks, local files, or extension APIs.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Publish capability-based support levels: universal core access, portable discovery, deterministic hook integration, optional memory harvest, and manual import for closed hosts.

questions.prompt: What belongs in the first implementation goal?
questions.description: This determines whether the work is a documentation correction or a complete integration-platform migration.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Include the adapter contract, backward-compatible configuration, native installer, portable skills, generic trust policy, safe write/JSON APIs, local stdio MCP, the three working integrations, a custom-host path, documentation, and contract/E2E tests. Defer remote servers and proprietary cloud-memory connectors.

questions.prompt: How strict should backward compatibility be?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Update the single live instance manually to the integration terminology and schema; do not carry automatic migration paths for historical formats.

questions.prompt: Which product integrations must be live-tested in this goal?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes remain the required live regression matrix; a synthetic custom host proves extensibility. Additional product presets can land later without changing the core contract.
